What a rule does in each direction

Source: R/rules.R
geoscale_rule_action.Rd

Every rule in GEOSCALE_RULES defines behaviour in both directions, and the direction follows the geoframe ranks. This reports, per rule, what going up and going down mean, and whether a parent's value is therefore divisible between its children: only sum is, because only sum splits a quantity. A rate, a price or a region-invariant scalar is replicated instead – the same value holds for every child – while sd and the two share rules have no downward meaning and are reported as NA rather than guessed at.

Usage

geoscale_rule_action(rule = GEOSCALE_RULES)

Arguments

rule

Character vector of rule names; defaults to every rule.

Value

A data.frame with one row per rule, in the order given, and columns rule, up, down, divisible (NA where the rule has no downward meaning) and action, one of "split", "replicate" or "none".

Details

A downstream package uses this to decide, column by column, what a partial selection of children does to a parent's value, without asking its caller.

Examples

geoscale_rule_action()
#>            rule                  up                               down
#> 1           sum                 sum split proportionally to the weight
#> 2 weighted_mean       weighted mean                               copy
#> 3          mean                mean                               copy
#> 4          copy    the common value                               copy
#> 5            sd  standard deviation                               <NA>
#> 6         share share within parent                               <NA>
#> 7      logshare share within parent                               <NA>
#>   divisible    action
#> 1      TRUE     split
#> 2     FALSE replicate
#> 3     FALSE replicate
#> 4     FALSE replicate
#> 5        NA      none
#> 6        NA      none
#> 7        NA      none
geoscale_rule_action("sum")$divisible
#> [1] TRUE
